messages:
Sam: Noticed a weird one during a demo — console showed another workspace's routes for ~2s after switching. Repro is pretty consistent when fast-switching tabs.
Elaine: yikes. any logs or repro steps?
Sam: Steps: 1) open console for tenant A, 2) hit routes page, 3) switch to tenant B quickly, 4) click refresh. Sometimes the list contains routes from A.
Jun: Could be ctx propagation + optimistic cache invalidation. We recently changed the fetch key to include only workspaceId in the UI, but the header we send is `x-rw-ctx` with session+route hints.
Matt: Do we reuse the same api-client instance across workspace switches? If so stale headers can bleed.
Sam: Yeah client is singleton. We set headers on each request, but there's a race where background polling doesn't pick up the new workspace id before the next render triggers a fetch.
Elaine: Can you paste the request/response when it happens?
Sam: here's a captured trace:
```
GET /api/console/routes?limit=50
Host: console.redwood.ai
x-rw-ctx: {"workspace":"A","session":"s-123"}
-> response: routes A
... quick switch ...
GET /api/console/routes?limit=50
x-rw-ctx: {"workspace":"B","session":"s-123"}
-> response: routes A  <-- server returned A despite header B
```
Jun: interesting — server saw workspace B but returned A. That suggests either routing policy used request path/param first and ignored header, or we have a cache layer keyed only by session.
Matt: our edge cache key was historically `session`+`routePath` for perf. If session stays same across workspaces, cache will return old body.
Elaine: oh no. that's a clear multi-tenant isolation hazard. We must never cache responses across workspace boundaries using a session-only key.
Sam: proposed quick mitigations: 1) add workspace to cache key at edge, 2) make adminConsole routes pass `Cache-Control: no-cache` temporarily for safety, 3) switch client to per-workspace fetcher instance.
Jun: +1 for #1 and #3. #2 is heavy but ok short-term. Also need a test that fuzzes rapid workspace switches.
Matt: worried about perf if we add workspace to every cache key — increases cardinality. But correctness trumps perf here. We can roll a smarter policy: only include workspace for console admin endpoints.
Elaine: agree. Also should log telemetry so we can detect cross-tenant hits automatically. Add an audit metric: cache_hit_workspace_mismatch (edge sees header workspace != cache_owner_workspace).
ops-bot: deploy-check: 2 pending PRs touching edge-cache config.
Sam: I'll open 2 PRs: one to add workspace to console cache key, and one to create a per-workspace api-client factory + test harness.
Jun: I'll own detection telemetry + the regression test that simulates rapid switches.
Matt: I'll file a follow-up to evaluate cache cardinality and an autoscaling knob if hit.
Elaine: also notify security and CS? This likely affected a small subset, but we should run a query on audit logs for any cross-workspace responses in the last 24h.
Sam: pinged security and cs via thread.
Jun: small API debate: should we rely on `x-rw-ctx` header as truth or canonicalize workspace from auth token at the gateway? Suggest the gateway derives workspace from JWT to avoid client header spoofing.
Matt: gateway canonicalization sounds safer. We'll need to ensure internal services trust gateway headers and strip client-provided ones.
Elaine: do that as follow-up — first patch triage: (a) stop caching across workspaces, (b) client per-workspace instance, (c) telemetry. Then gateway canonicalization next week.
Sam: created PRs and added manual rollback steps. tagging: @Jun @Matt @Elaine :eyes:
ops-bot: deploy started: edge-config update (staged) -> rolling.
Sam: thank you — will monitor metrics and post back if anything else shows up.
